newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta group plans for 40/50 hotels in seven years.
newsitem.headline: Malta group plans for 40/50 hotels in seven years.

text.p: Malta's Corinthia hotels group is planning rapid international expansion with the acquisition or construction of between 40 and 50 hotels within seven years, chairman Alfred Pisani said in remarks published on Friday.

Pisani told the Maltese newspaper the Times: "Hopefully in between five and seven years' time, we will have a chain of between 40 and 50 hotels, which will make us a real force to be reckoned with internationally."

The group has four hotels in Malta, three in Turkey and one in Hungary. It is planning to build a second hotel in Hungary, another in Istanbul and a fifth in Malta. A Corinthia hotel will open in Tunis in July and talks are being held on building a five-star hotel in Libya.
Pisani said his group would concentrate mainly in the former communist countries near Hungary and former Soviet countries near Turkey.
"Both these markets are set for massive growth and operators who get in now will be carried along on this wave of expansion," Pisani said.
"Our bases in Turkey and Hungary will help us tap these markets."
The Corinthia group started with a restaurant in 1962 followed shortly after by the five-star Corinthia Palace Hotel.
Pisani said its expansion has been made possible by meticulous financial planning and the timing of its move into Turkey, while prices were still low.
He said he had not ruled out flotation on the stock exchange but did not see much benefit for the company at the moment.
